name: Spodumene ore
notes: Typical Li2O grade 1.0–2.0%; primary hard-rock lithium source (Australia, Canada)

name: Spodumene concentrate
notes: Upgraded to ~6% Li2O; feedstock for chemical conversion

name: Lithium brine (raw)
notes: Li concentration ~0.05–0.15% by weight; evaporite deposits (Atacama, Qinghai)

name: Lithium carbonate
notes: Battery-grade ≥99.5%; primary feedstock for LFP; also intermediate for LiOH

name: Lithium hydroxide monohydrate
notes: Battery-grade ≥56.5% LiOH; preferred for high-Ni NMC (≥NMC622) and NCA

name: Nickel laterite ore
notes: Typical Ni grade 1.0–2.0%; dominant ore type globally; processed via HPAL or pyrometallurgy

name: Nickel sulfide ore
notes: Typical Ni grade 0.5–3%; lower processing cost than laterite; declining share of supply

name: Nickel sulfate solution (battery-grade)
notes: Battery-grade ≥22% Ni; primary feedstock for NMC/NCA precursor co-precipitation

name: Cobalt-bearing ore (Cu-Co)
notes: Typical Co grade 0.1–0.5%; predominantly DRC; cobalt is byproduct of copper mining

name: Cobalt sulfate solution (battery-grade)
notes: Battery-grade ≥20% Co; feedstock for NMC/NCA precursor

name: Manganese ore
notes: Typical Mn grade 25–50%; major producers: South Africa, Australia, Gabon

name: Manganese sulfate solution (battery-grade)
notes: Battery-grade; feedstock for NMC precursor and LMO/LMFP

name: Iron phosphate (battery-grade)
notes: Primary LFP precursor; can be synthesized via wet chemical or hydrothermal route

name: Iron oxalate
notes: Alternative LFP precursor; used in some solid-state synthesis routes

name: Phosphate rock
notes: Raw phosphorus source; concentrated to phosphoric acid before use

name: Phosphoric acid (battery-grade)
notes: Used in wet-chemical LFP precursor synthesis

name: NMC811 hydroxide precursor
notes: Co-precipitated from NiSO4/CoSO4/MnSO4 solution; d50 typically 10–15 µm

name: LFP iron phosphate precursor
notes: Standard precursor for solid-state LFP synthesis

name: NMC811 cathode active material
notes: Calcined from PCAM_NMC811 + LiOH; tap density ~2.2 g/cc; single or polycrystalline

name: LFP cathode active material (standard)
notes: Conventional solid-state synthesis; d50 ~2–5 µm; electrode density ~2.2–2.4 g/cc

name: LFP cathode active material (nano, high compaction)
notes: Hydrothermal/nano synthesis; d50 ~0.2–0.8 µm; carbon-coated; electrode density up to 2.5–2.6 g/cc

name: Natural graphite (spheronized, purified)
notes: Spheronized from flake graphite; purified to >99.95% C; primary anode for LIBs

name: Synthetic graphite
notes: Graphitized from petroleum coke at ~3000°C; higher purity, higher cost/energy than natural

name: Natural flake graphite (mined)
notes: Raw mined graphite before spheronization; typical C content 85–95%

name: Lithium hexafluorophosphate
notes: Primary Li-salt in conventional electrolyte; ~1M concentration in carbonate solvents

name: Liquid electrolyte (bulk, formulated)
notes: LiPF6 in EC/DMC or EC/EMC/DMC; typically 2.0–2.8 g/Ah at cell level

name: Aluminum foil (cathode current collector)
notes: Thickness 12–16 µm; battery-grade purity ≥99.9%

name: Copper foil (anode current collector)
notes: Thickness 6–10 µm; electrolytic copper; major cost and supply chain concern

name: Separator (polyolefin)
notes: PE, PP, or trilayer PE/PP/PE; thickness 12–25 µm; may include ceramic coating
